note: Independent re-audit against RFC 6396 Section 4.2 ("The TABLE_DUMP Type does not permit 4-byte Peer AS numbers, nor does it allow the AFI of the peer IP to differ from the AFI of the Prefix field.  The TABLE_DUMP_V2 Type MUST be used in these situations."). Re-read writeTableDumpV2 and writePeerIndexTable after commits d07e4dc944 and 4db24861ee: both OnRoute and OnRouteAddPath share the single writeRoute closure, which unconditionally stamps TypeTableDumpV2 for every PEER_INDEX_TABLE and RIB record (unicast, multicast, generic, with or without ADD-PATH) and encodes every peer entry with PeerAS4 (plus PeerIPv6 when IPv6). Both tagged tests (TestDumpV2PeerWidthAndPrefixFamily and supplementary TestRibSubtype) remain strong: TestDumpV2PeerWidthAndPrefixFamily drives Component.writeTableDumpV2 end-to-end across all eight combinations of IPv4/IPv6 peer, IPv4/IPv6 prefix, and 2-byte/4-byte peer ASN (65001 / 0x01020304), asserting TypeTableDumpV2 on every MRT header before body dispatch, exact PIT/RIB counts and subtypes, exact 4-byte ASN/IP/BGPID in the decoded PIT, and exact sequence/prefix/peer index/attributes in the decoded RIB. The {single-polarity: positive} annotation remains justified because Ze's RIB dump path never emits deprecated TABLE_DUMP (Type 12). Verdict: enforced.
